title: Workspace Doorway Access Patterns and Cost‑Lens Previews
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Redesign the console's primary left rail and workspace switching surface to surface a lightweight 'doorway' pattern: a compact vertical access panel that opens contextual previews, inline cost lenses, and fast switch affordances. Goals: reduce time-to-switch between workspaces by at least 30%, make cost implications visible before route navigation, and provide safe rollouts for canary vs production routes. Deliverables: high-fidelity Figma prototype (desktop/tablet), annotated IA map, interaction spec for dev, and usability testing report with 8 tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Left rail compresses to doorway glyphs at 240px content width and expands on hover or keyboard focus
Workspace preview shows last 5 routes, active model, and token cost estimate for most-recent route
Cost‑lens overlays surface per-route token breakdown and a tip to open Optimize suggestions
Keyboard-first navigation: Win/Linux and macOS shortcuts to open previews and confirm switch
Prototype validated with 6 product-engineer reviewers and 8 usability participants showing >75% success rate
Edge-case behaviors documented: multi-tenant contexts, restricted workspaces, and mobile fallback
design_decisions: Doorway pattern chosen over full-width flyout to reduce visual noise and prioritize primary content
Preview content limited to 3–5 high-value items (routes, models, recent queries) to keep latency and rendering predictable
Cost estimates use cached last-known token profile, with a CTA to fetch a fresh estimate asynchronously to avoid blocking UI
Rollout uses feature-flag + canary group mapping in Console: quick fallback to legacy sidebar if latency > 200ms
Accessibility: previews are ARIA-dialogs with focus trap and clear escape handling for screen readers
